Package io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api

package io.github.wurtzitane.avogadro.api
Builds, registers, and looks up molecule definitions. Safe to use on a client or a dedicated server.

New here? Start with your first molecule, browse the rendered examples, or use the field and recipe tables.

See chirality and R/S and SMILES, external groups, radicals and geometry constraints for the complete authoring examples and in-game previews.

Register a molecule

A builder describes the molecule. Registration makes it available in the game: 

var water = AvogadroApi.builder("example:water")
    .name("Water")
    .smiles("O");
AvogadroApi.owner("example").register(water);

The owner name groups your registrations so you can update or remove your own definitions later. Use AvogadroApi.serverView() for server decisions. Use the separate client API when you need to respect client resource overrides.

Build a shape from parts

  • A fragment is a piece of a molecule: atoms, positions, and bonds.
  • An attachment gives an atom a name, such as head or tail, so other parts can connect to it.
  • An assembly is a recipe that places fragments, repeats them, and adds bonds between them.
  • A polymer network uses an assembly with adjustable counts or chances of adding branches and crosslinks.

For example, these calls create a two-atom fragment with named ends: 

StructureFragment part = new StructureBuilder()
    .atom("C", 0, 0, 0)
    .atom("O", 1.4, 0, 0)
    .bond(0, 1)
    .attachment("head", 0)
    .attachment("tail", 1)
    .build();

Atoms and bonds must be supplied by the author. Assembly operations do not optimize positions or repair chemical bonding. Editing returns a new result, leaving the original fragment unchanged.
